risks.message: Row locks (FOR UPDATE/SHARE) only hold inside one transaction; lock and subsequent writes must share the same connection/transaction.

recommendations.message: Keep joins, aggregates, CTEs and bulk DML as parameterized SQL.
Receive an open connection; do not commit inside the function.
Map RAISE EXCEPTION to typed exceptions and RAISE NOTICE to logging.

architectural_decisions.decision: The function receives an open AsyncConnection and never commits; the FOR UPDATE selects and all dependent writes run on that same connection/transaction.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Row locks only hold within the caller's transaction; the original procedure also relied on the surrounding transaction.

architectural_decisions.decision: The protected writes run inside `async with conn.begin_nested():` and the handler (audit insert + re-raise) runs outside it.
architectural_decisions.rationale: A PL/pgSQL BEGIN...EXCEPTION block is a savepoint; without the nested savepoint the transaction would be aborted and the error-log insert would fail.

architectural_decisions.decision: p_valor is bound as unconstrained NUMERIC everywhere (never NUMERIC(18,2)); the NUMERIC(18,2) saldo/valor columns perform the final rounding on assignment.
architectural_decisions.rationale: The original variable is plain NUMERIC: `saldo - 0.005` is computed at full precision and the column assignment rounds half-away-from-zero (200 - 0.005 -> 200.00). Pre-casting the bind to NUMERIC(18,2) would round 0.005 to 0.01 first and change the resulting balance and the JSON detalhes.

architectural_decisions.decision: Each RAISE EXCEPTION became a typed exception subclassing TransferenciaError; the WHEN OTHERS handler logs via logging and re-raises.
architectural_decisions.rationale: Typed exceptions preserve the original error semantics for callers while keeping the audit-on-error behaviour.

warnings: The transacoes.valor column is NUMERIC(18,2), so a transfer of 0.005 is stored there as 0.01 by the column itself (same as the original); the audit-log detalhes.valor keeps the full 0.005 because it is cast to unconstrained NUMERIC.

The error-log insert in the WHEN OTHERS handler runs on the caller's transaction; if the caller rolls back the whole transaction afterwards, that audit row is rolled back too (identical to the original procedure's behaviour).
SQLERRM is approximated by str(exc) of the Python exception; the message text may differ slightly from PostgreSQL's formatted error string.
The saldo-insufficient and status checks read values locked by FOR UPDATE on the same connection, so no lost-update race is introduced by moving the comparisons to Python.
